central_hypothesis: a public uniform poly(log n) exact parity evaluator exists

audited_results.V1: linear translation-stable modules with linear readout require dimension n
audited_results.V2: low-pole rational state plus low-degree polynomial readout needs composite pole budget at least (n-1)/2
audited_results.V3: an r-mode translation-spectral state with degree-d polynomial readout requires binomial(r+d,d)>=n
audited_results.V4: the local odd-cycle equation is only an elementary implicit characterization, not algorithmic compression
audited_results.V5: no formula tree of size at most four in the tiny declared coordinate-rational grammar matches parity on the five-curve toy corpus
audited_results.V6: any exact state with one fixed linear or affine update over F_(p^d), even with an arbitrary decoder, requires d*r>=ord_n(p) or d*(r+1)>=ord_n(p)

secp256k1_V6.consequence: fixed autonomous linear, affine, and Mobius state transports cannot have poly(log n) base-field dimension

not_proved: existence of a classical polynomial-time parity algorithm
existence of a practically fast parity algorithm
nonexistence of a classical polynomial-time parity algorithm
next_admitted_class: nonlinear coordinate-dependent or query-dependent random-access state evolution, including high-degree low-DAG-size circuits and modular-composition jump-ahead mechanisms
